title: 2026 U.S. House of Representatives election in Colorado's 5th Congressional District
description: Colorado's 5th Congressional District, centered on Colorado Springs and El Paso County, is an increasingly competitive Republican-leaning district. Incumbent Republican Jeff Crank, first elected in 2024 with 54.7% of the vote, is running for re-election and is unopposed in the Republican primary. Two Democrats, Jessica Killin and Joe Reagan, are competing in the June 30 Democratic primary to face Crank in November, while independent candidate Steven Fuller has also qualified for the general election ballot. The Cook Political Report rates the seat as 'Solid R,' though the district has trended left in recent presidential cycles and national Democrats have added it to their target lists.
polling_note: Only one poll was identified: an internal Democratic poll from November 2025 showing a narrow 3-point lead for incumbent Jeff Crank over Democrat Jessica Killin, within the margin of error. No independent or media-sponsored polls were publicly available as of mid-June 2026.

candidates.name: Jeff Crank
candidates.summary: Jeff Crank is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Colorado's 5th Congressional District, first elected in 2024. A former radio talk show host and longtime conservative activist, he previously served as Colorado state director for Americans for Prosperity and worked as a congressional staffer for Representative Joel Hefley. Crank has been endorsed by President Donald Trump and serves on the House Armed Services and Natural Resources Committees.

candidates.name: Jessica Killin
candidates.summary: Jessica Killin is a Democratic candidate for Colorado's 5th Congressional District and a fourth-generation Coloradan. She is a former U.S. Army captain and paratrooper who served as a Military Police Officer in peacekeeping missions, later worked as an executive at USAA supporting military families, and served as chief of staff to former Second Gentleman Doug Emhoff. Killin has been endorsed by Senators Michael Bennet and John Hickenlooper and national Democratic organizations, and her campaign has raised record sums for a Democrat in this district.

candidates.name: Steven Fuller
candidates.summary: Steven Fuller is an independent (Unaffiliated) candidate for Colorado's 5th Congressional District. He is a 14-year U.S. Army combat veteran with three tours in Iraq and the founder and head brewer of Wackadoo Brewing in Colorado Springs, which donates 100% of its profits to charity. Fuller was named the 2025 Veteran Entrepreneur of the Year for Colorado District 5 and has pledged to support congressional term limits.

forecast.rationale: Republicans remain favored based on the district's Republican lean (Cook 'Solid R'), Jeff Crank's incumbency, his 54.7% win in 2024, and his uncontested primary status. However, competitive signals are emerging: the only available poll (a Democratic internal from Nov 2025) shows a narrow 43%-40% race within the margin of error; Democrat Jessica Killin has raised record funds and earned endorsements from Senators Bennet and Hickenlooper; national Democrats have added the district to target lists; and the district has trended left in recent presidential cycles. The Democratic primary is still unresolved as of June 20 (concluding June 30), adding further uncertainty. Independent candidate Steven Fuller introduces a potential third-way vote. With only one old partisan poll and no independent polling, confidence is moderate — the Republican edge is clear but not overwhelming, and the margin could narrow significantly depending on the eventual Democratic nominee and general election dynamics.
